correctness.rationale: For every infinite set Γ (including noncountable Γ) over complex scalars, the isometric direct limit T of c0(Γ) even duals has canonical positive layer E=ℓ∞(Γ). The norm-one fiber lemma is exact: for a unital norm-one projection C(L)→π* C(K), evaluation on u gives a positive probability µ supported in π^-1(u). On a fiber with three points one point y has µ{y}≤1/3, and ||δ_y−µ||=2(1−µ{y})≥4/3. The decomposition C(βΓ)*=ℓ1(Γ)⊕1 M(U), U=βΓ\Γ, dualizes to the central C*-direct sum E**=ℓ∞(Γ)⊕∞ C(U)** with canonical JE(f)=(f,J_C(U)(f|U)). The induced spectrum surjection K⊔L_C(U)→K fixes K and maps second-spectrum fibers onto U. C(U) contains an isometric c0 via infinitely many pairwise disjoint nonempty clopen subsets of U, hence is nonreflexive; the second-spectrum map has a non-singleton fiber, which together with the fixed K point produces ≥3 points. Restricting a tower P to E** transfers the complement-norm lower bound. Compatible canonical adjoints (J_X(2n−1))* supply a norm-one retraction onto E, so the bounded class is nonempty. No finite test is used as infinite proof; the 4/3 is a lower bound and may not be sharp for the tower.

Baker and Wolfe, Averaging operators and C(X)-spaces with the separable projection property, Canadian J. Math. 28 (1976), 897–904, Theorem 1 and Lemma 4. Estimates projection norms for compact surjections in a metrizable setting; its invariant is the norm of Q rather than the complement norm I−Q.

The tower claim needs both an explicit triple fiber in the canonical Gelfand spectrum map E**→E and the 4/3 total-variation estimate for all norm-one retractions.

A bicontractive projection is one-half the identity plus a surjective order-two isometry; this gives qualitative restrictions on C(K) fibers.
An M-projection is bicontractive, but a bicontractive projection need not be an M-projection; thus no M-projection does not imply no bicontractive projection.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality for the full quantitative tower-layer statement, not for the general bicontractive obstruction or projection construction. Liu–Uglešić Proposition 4.1 only prohibits the stronger M-projection and expressly says the weaker bicontractive property is unsettled. Friedman–Russo gives a powerful prior order-two-isometry classification of bicontractive projections on C*-algebras: combined with newly identifying a fiber of size at least three, it already implies qualitative non-bicontractivity; the qualitative mechanism is thus strongly anticipated. Neither inspected theorem supplies the uniform numerical bound ||I−P||≥4/3 for every norm-one tower-layer projection. The contribution that survives these logical implications is the explicit positive quantitative norm gap for the canonical c0(Γ) tower and the structural triple-fiber proof, for all infinite Γ. Priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: The prior Friedman–Russo/Stormer involution theorem already gives the qualitative non-bicontractivity obstruction once triple fibers are recognized. The present bound may be judged a relatively elementary quantitative corollary, reducing priority significance.
An older general theorem on complements of unital C(K) subalgebras could state ||I−Q||≥2(1−1/m) for fibers of cardinality m; this was not ruled out exhaustively.
The optimal complement norm for the full completed tower may exceed 4/3; sharpness is not claimed.
Publication/database absence is not proof of originality; unindexed sources and terminology changes remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The natural structural question singled out by Liu–Uglešić is whether a canonical positive bidual-tower layer can be both contractively and bicontractively complemented. The explicit 4/3 complementary operator-norm gap, valid for every infinite Γ, quantitatively separates contractive complementation from bicontractivity and therefore resolves the c0-family instance of that open distinction. The spectrum-fiber geometry and uniform cardinality independence explain a genuine Banach-space obstruction. The general existence of norm-one projections and qualitative involution theorem are not counted as novel independent contributions. The exact optimal gap for the full tower, higher positive layers, real analogues, and arbitrary X are left open.
